review.summary: Phase 19 "typed preservation" chunk (attempt 5/5) delivers the plan's item-3 obligation correctly and with real, executed evidence. The generator (tools/generate_models.py:471-506) emits a hand-written Deserialize for the 25 models carrying vendor-added fields: each projection key is removed from the raw map, decoded through the bounded crate::json_decode path, and on failure re-inserted so the baseline flatten carries it into Extensions with the typed projection left unset; the matching Serialize suppresses the extension only when the typed field is explicitly set, so no duplicate JSON keys are produced, while baseline-field extension collisions still fail closed. A generator guard rejects any non-optional projection (tools/generate_models.py:472), so the vendor cannot silently widen a baseline requirement. Coverage is derived, not hand-picked: contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json enumerates all 55 added fields with nullability, a schema-derived conforming witness and request/response usage, and tools/g25_fixtures.py:421-541 regenerates the Rust match arms so an unbound model or field panics. The Rust suite exercises every field in both response modes against absence, null, wrong-type, nested-object and array values (g25_response_compatibility.rs:404-428), asserts actual typed state plus extension presence (1067-1100), proves typed-over-raw precedence and baseline collision failure (511-533), covers u128-range numbers for every projection model and a nested union branch (1102-1146), and the whole 15,658-case corpus is round-tripped through the public parse of each operation's real result type (61-130). red_team_contracts.rs:2478-2600 drives typed attack lists, target-profile error logs and the runtime-profile decoder exemption through the actual client transport in both modes with job-1/p-1/map-1 and both timestamp forms. The recorded gate receipt (docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-typed-preservation-attempt-05.checks.json) is an exact, in-order execution of tools/check_phase.py commands_for(19): all 27 commands exit 0 on source 22764b5…, including generate_models --check, g25_fixtures --check, the full oracle/contract suites, and six check-rust runs covering red-team and the new red-team-json-unification combination on both 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 — the combination is wired into the 24x2+1 = 49-job matrix and pinned by tools/test_ci.py:111-127. Importantly, vendor augmentation is confined to model generation; generate_validation.py does not call augment_models, so request validation keeps the exact frozen/vendor constraints. Deficiencies are documentation-level, not functional: the generated compatibility report names only the three JobCreateRequest* models as request-side, omitting the eight request-reachable TargetMetadata/LanguageOption projections, and the guard test pins only the "request-only" subset; CI's contracts gate does not yet execute the G25 generator/oracle checks (phase 20 scope). No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: The generated compatibility report hardcodes the request-side typed-over-raw disclosure to `JobCreateRequestJobMetadataVariant1/2/3`, but contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json classifies eight further projections on request-reachable models as "request-and-response" (TargetMetadata: audio_probe_passed, audio_probe_error, audio_multi_turn_probe_passed, audio_multi_turn_probe_error, supports_audio, audio_format, supports_text; LanguageOption: country_code) and two as "standalone-schema" (ValidationError.input, ValidationError.ctx). A caller who sets both a typed TargetMetadata.supports_audio and an extension with the same wire key gets the extension silently omitted on request serialization — exactly the behavior the paragraph claims to disclose — yet that model is not named. The rendered text at docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:17 therefore under-reports a caller-visible request-side behavior change, and the list is prose rather than derived from the ledger it links, so it will drift on the next vendor update.
findings.required_fix: Derive the request-side model list in tools/g25_report.py from projections.json rows whose usage is "request-only" or "request-and-response" (and state the standalone-schema models separately), then regenerate docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md.

findings.description: test_vendor_string_bounds_are_request_only pins the request-side projection inventory to `{r["rustType"] for r in rows if r["usage"] == "request-only"}`, i.e. only the three JobCreateRequest* variants. Nothing asserts the "request-and-response" or "standalone-schema" sets, so the incomplete report prose above has no guard and a future vendor addition to TargetMetadata, LanguageOption or another request-reachable model would be accepted with no documentation update and no test failure.
findings.required_fix: Extend the assertion to pin the full usage partition (request-only, request-and-response, standalone-schema, response-only) and assert that every request-reachable model named by the generated report matches that derived set.

findings.description: rustfmt is resolved as `shutil.which("rustfmt") or ~/.cargo/bin/rustfmt` and then invoked as `[rustfmt, "+1.99.0", "--edition", "2024"]`. If the rustfmt found on PATH is a real rustfmt rather than a rustup proxy, `+1.99.0` is consumed as a path argument and the run fails with an opaque error; because rust_bindings() formats on every invocation, `--check` (a phase-19 gate command) also hard-depends on a rustup-proxied toolchain rather than only the regeneration path.
findings.required_fix: Verify the resolved binary accepts a toolchain selector (or detect the rustup proxy) before passing `+1.99.0`, and raise an explicit diagnostic naming the required toolchain when it does not.

findings.description: The contracts-and-package job runs `tools/check_phase.py --phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only`, whose command set (check_phase.py:487-498 filtering commands_for(17)) does not include `tools/g25_fixtures.py --check`, `tools/g25_report.py --check` or `tools/g25-oracle.mts --check`. Drift between the generators and the committed cases/outcomes/projections/ledger is therefore caught only by the local phase-19 gate; CI catches it only indirectly through test_g25*.py in-process regeneration and the Rust corpus assertions. The plan assigns this wiring to phase 20, so this is an accepted carry-forward rather than a missing chunk deliverable.
findings.required_fix: In phase 20, add the three G25 `--check` commands to the CI contracts gate while preserving the historical command lists, and bind the addition in tools/test_ci.py.

findings.description: Every projection model collapses a baseline decode failure to the single redacted message "baseline response model mismatch" (emitted by tools/generate_models.py:495). Redaction is deliberate — serde's error text can echo response data — but the message carries no field name, so a genuine baseline contract break in production yields no actionable signal beyond the model name.
findings.required_fix: Consider emitting the offending baseline field name only (never its value), for example by attempting the baseline decode field-by-field on failure, so operators can localize a contract break without exposing service data.

findings.description: Union pairing selects the vendor variant with `max(candidates, key=overlap)`; ties are resolved by iteration order, so a vendor-added field can be attached to the wrong object variant of a union. The blast radius is contained — a misplaced optional typed projection simply stays unset and the raw value is preserved in extensions — and other mappings fail closed (test_g25_generation.test_ambiguous_mapping_fails_closed), but this particular selection does not. The file is listed under the validation-policy chunk, though its `additions` output is this chunk's input.
findings.required_fix: Fail closed (or record an explicit reviewed override) when two or more candidate variants tie on property overlap, instead of silently taking the first maximum.
